outcome: Performance problems traced to the exact network segment or provider responsible, turning provider disputes into evidence-based conversations.
overview: When a software company’s service is slow for customers in one country, the internal monitoring usually shows everything green, because the problem is in a path nobody owns. ThousandEyes measures from vantage points across the internet and inside the estate, so a degradation can be attributed to a specific provider, region or peering point. The value is almost entirely diplomatic: it converts an argument with a provider into a conversation about evidence, and it tells a support team quickly when the fault is genuinely not theirs.

benefits.text: A performance problem can be attributed to a specific network segment rather than assumed internal
benefits.limits: Attribution identifies where the degradation is; it does not create leverage over a provider who is unwilling to act on it

benefits.text: Customer-experienced performance is measured from where customers actually are
benefits.limits: Vantage points approximate customer locations; they are not the customers’ own devices and should not be described as real-user measurement

benefits.text: Support engineers can rule the network in or out early instead of investigating in the dark
benefits.limits: Value depends on the data reaching the support process; a dashboard nobody consults during an incident changes nothing

residency: Measurement results are held in the vendor’s platform; test configuration and results leave the customer estate and the tenant region is recorded at design

notFor.situation: A company already running internet-path monitoring with an established process
notFor.why: A second measurement source produces disagreement rather than clarity unless one is retired

notFor.situation: A service used only inside one corporate network
notFor.why: There is no internet path to measure
